title: B9909G corn (Bioseed 9909): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: B9909G corn: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: B9909G corn is a yellow GM hybrid corn variety for Mindanao. About 100 days to harvest, 8.2 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: B9909G corn is a yellow GM hybrid corn variety, also sold or known as Bioseed 9909 or Bioseed 9909G. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2015 as NSIC 2015 GMCn 38. Bioseed Research bred it. It takes about 100 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain, with 8.24 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Bioseed 9909 or Bioseed 9909G, this is the same corn. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [corn variety finder](/crop-varieties/corn), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Pagtatanim ng mais, step by step](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-mais).

items: **Days to harvest:** about 100 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain.
**Yield:** 8.24 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

B9909G corn takes about 100 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. That is 4.9 days faster than the average of the 89 yellow GM hybrid corn varieties with a day count, 105.4 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 8.24 t/ha matches the average of its group, 8.13. One tonne of shelled corn fills about 20 sacks of 50 kilograms. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 100 in NSIC trials.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [Corn rust](/diseases/corn-rust), [Corn stalk rot](/diseases/corn-stalk-rot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm).

The pests and diseases that hit corn fields most often: [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [banded leaf and sheath blight](/diseases/banded-leaf-and-sheath-blight), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn ear rot](/diseases/corn-ear-rot), [Corn planthopper](/pests/corn-planthopper). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

Its ears grew about 18.03 cm long in the trials. The shelling recovery was 76 percent, the share of the ear weight that comes off as grain. A higher share means more grain from every sack of ears. Against lodging it rated resistant, so it stood up well when wind and rain pushed the plants.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** Isabela farmers reported about 8.5 t/ha in a normal season and still 5 to 7 t/ha in a 45 day drought, NSIC trials averaged 8.24 t/ha (GM version), 7.27 t/ha for the conventional Bioseed 9909.

**Traits in the seed:** VT Double PRO (events MON89034 x NK603): two built in insect protection genes against Asian corn borer, earworm and armyworms, plus glyphosate (Roundup) tolerance, 95:5 refuge seed blend.
Known locally for holding yield in drought.
Registry rates it resistant to lodging, corn borer, rust, stalk rot and earworm.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: an older Bioseed hybrid with a loyal following in Isabela for drought hardiness, still entered by Bioseed as B9909G in DA Northern Mindanao derbies in 2023. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant B9909G corn

The registry recommends it for Mindanao. It suits lowland areas. Start with the color your buyer pays for: yellow corn goes to feed mills, while white and glutinous corn go to the table. Next, pick between a hybrid, which yields more but needs new seed every season, and an open pollinated variety, whose seed you can save. Then match the island group in its recommendation, because trials in Luzon and Mindanao give different winners. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for corn](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items.q: Is Bioseed 9909 the same as B9909G?
items.a: Yes. Bioseed 9909 is another name for B9909G, registered as NSIC 2015 GMCn 38. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 100 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 8.24 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.
The registry recommends it for Mindanao. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of B9909G?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
